plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: Towering stalks carry huge golden blooms that follow the sun across the sky. In the fields of the northern Great Plains, whole hillsides glow yellow, with dark chocolate-brown centers buzzing with bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (roughly July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: North American Great Plains, such as Kansas and the Dakotas, USA
plants.funFact: What looks like one flower is actually a composite head of hundreds to thousands of tiny florets. The seeds form in a spiral pattern that follows the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes of fragrant violet-blue flowers. In the lavender fields of Provence, the purple rows hum with pollinators and perfume the warm summer air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (about June to August) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Provence, southern France, and other Mediterranean-climate regions
plants.funFact: Lavender's name probably comes from the Latin word for washing, because the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: In the Australian winter, this hardy tree bursts into clouds of fluffy, golden pom-pom flowers with a honeyed scent. It brightens the cool landscapes of southeastern Australia when little else is in color.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (about July to October) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem. National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.
